description: Use when the user wants to list or inspect documents in Stuga, including indirect requests about “the doc” or “my workspace”; they do not need to name this tool or MCP. action: list (documents you can reach in the workspace; `parent_id` lists one folder, null the root) | metadata (one document, `doc_id`) | index | log | lint. metadata reports `review`: whether a write to THIS document would wait for the user or apply at once, and why — read it before writing when the answer would change your plan; `linked_from`, the pages that link to or cite it; and `needs_checking`, pages it cites that changed after it was approved. metadata and `docs_create` return the standing `instructions` people set for that document, outermost first — follow them when writing there. To find documents by what they say, use `search`. index: the wiki's table of contents, by folder (`parent_id` narrows it to one): each page's title, `summary` (its opening paragraph), when its approved text last changed and who changed it, and `needs_checking`; each database's `rows` and its last change. log: the AI changes people approved or declined, newest first: what changed where (a database's `tables` and the rows touched), who asked, who decided, when; pass `next` back as `before` for older ones. Both are generated; neither is a page to write to. lint: check the wiki, when the user says "Check Stuga" or the same in their language ("检查 Stuga", "檢查 Stuga", "Stugaをチェック", "Stuga 점검", "Stuga prüfen", "Vérifier Stuga", "Revisar Stuga", "Verificar o Stuga"), or asks what in it is out of date or broken (`parent_id` checks one folder): pages that need checking because a page they cite changed since, orphans no other page links to, and broken links, a link to a deleted row of a table among them (`row_deleted`). Fix NOTHING by rewriting a page: propose each fix as a small edit, all of them in ONE change for the user's approval, and tell the user what you proposed and what you left for them to decide; a `not_found` link may name a page the user cannot open, so never take one out unasked; marking a page checked is a person's, never yours.

before.description: log: the `next` an earlier page of the log gave, for the entries before it.

limit.description: log: entries to return, 20 by default.

workspace_id.description: The workspace to act in: a `workspace_id` from `workspaces` action:list, which also says which node it is on.
